answer: One agent registers one pet with the municipal registry and ties the registration number to a single identity. A lotus of fake identities needs an inlet of paperwork: three established peers check the number in the public pet registry, the vet record, and a fresh signature. Registration costs $15 to $50 plus the pet itself and a vet visit, so a thousand fakes burns $15,000 to $50,000 and a thousand pets, each one waiting on a separate vet appointment. The registration renews yearly. Like shale under a garden path, one registration ties one agent to one record no one else can claim.
